comparator.name: Communicatie- en Informatiewetenschappen
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official curriculum totals 180 ECTS: 60 ECTS of common communication and academic-skills courses in year 1; 30 ECTS of philosophy, programming and research methods plus 24 ECTS in one theme and a 6-ECTS elective in year 2; and a 30-ECTS minor or exchange window, 18 ECTS of structured choice and a 12-ECTS bachelor thesis in year 3. The generic registry target does not name one of the six themes, so the first-listed theme, Bedrijfscommunicatie, is instantiated by neutral official-order tie-break. Open minor and compulsory-choice space remains open rather than being populated with assumed courses.
components: Genuinely open mobility or minor space.
Structured choice among a second theme, an internship plus theme courses, or courses from other themes.

alternatives.label: Communication, organisations & digital media
alternatives.concept: A broad communication curriculum joining rhetoric and media analysis to organisational communication, marketing, digital systems and empirical research. It responds to the common Tilburg core and the selected Corporate Communication theme without claiming the full specialist sequence or required thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines communication and persuasion, organisational and marketing contexts, digital media and empirical research; the label makes the three principal strands visible without presenting UCR as the specialist Tilburg degree.
progression: Rhetoric, business, data and research foundations precede advanced persuasion, market research, organisational psychology and digital study; all formal prerequisites are earlier and semester availability is satisfied.

alternatives.label: Communication for social impact
alternatives.concept: A public communication route connecting rhetoric and media analysis with climate, health, social movements, environmental justice and civil society. Its empirical and organisational courses support scrutiny of persuasive messages and communication for change.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed courses have sustained public, climate, health and social-justice content alongside communication theory and methods, so the social-impact label describes the curricular priority.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad programme, this route replaces nine courses in business, marketing, data and AI with climate, public health, media representation, social movements, environmental justice and civil-society study; those differences follow the evidenced social-impact direction.
progression: Introductory rhetoric, sociology, climate and public-health foundations precede analysis of environmental media, social movements, persuasion and advanced civil-society study. The research and business gateway precedes all dependent courses, and assigned terms match availability.

alternatives.label: Human and digital communication
alternatives.concept: A digital communication route examining social media, persuasive texts, human language processing and the behaviour and ethics of AI systems. It combines programming, data and visual methods with communication research and human-centred concerns.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines rhetorical communication with media and human language study and substantial AI, programming and data analysis, so both human and digital elements are visible.
alternatives.distinctness: This route substitutes specialised programming, AI decision-making, neural networks, visual analysis, psycholinguistics and philosophy of mind for much of the broad programme's international business, marketing, organisational psychology and qualitative-methods strand. It also differs from the social-impact route by a sustained technical and cognitive sequence.
progression: Communication, business and data foundations precede digital transformation and advanced rhetoric; mathematical methods and programming precede neural networks and AI optimisation, and brain and behaviour precedes psycholinguistics. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names the generic Communicatie- en Informatiewetenschappen bachelor and does not privilege one of its six equal-status themes. Bedrijfscommunicatie is the first theme listed on the official programme page, so it is selected before comparison with UCR and independently of UCR fit.

selection.assessment: The broad route covers communication theory, organisations, media, persuasion and research. Social-impact communication and human/digital communication have independently evidenced organising logics and materially different course selections. The optional Dutch-language teacher-preparation route is a further stable direction, but no fourth programme can be included.

notes.text: Tilburg requires sustained communication research, a 24-ECTS thematic sequence, academic-language work and a 12-ECTS bachelor thesis. UCR can combine rhetoric, media, organisational study, social issues and digital methods in several coherent ways, but these schedules do not reproduce that full specialist sequence.
